title: Gaspar's, the opera conductor, and his unrecorded family of musicians
summary: Playing intermission at Gaspar's, he saw the friend astonish an opera conductor; he never recorded, from a musical family.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I worked in intermission. I was playing intermission for him at Gaspar's on Bourbon Street. And they had an opera at one of the places in New Orleans. And the conductor came after. And Gaspar knew Bourbon, the man who owned the place was Gaspar. He knew Bourbon could play. And he came up and told Bourbon, he said, here's a long-haired guy. And he said, I want you to play something for him. And Bourbon played a classic that the man jumped up and said it can't be done. Honest. He said it just can't be done. A man just can't play that good.
That's how great he was. That's right.
And so many people came band, Duke Ellington's band and them used to come through and hear him playing want to take him just as a soloist, but he never would leave. He was, man he was a genius.
Yeah. Never made a record or anything?

Never made none, no records or nothing. It's really pitiful. Of course Bourbon was gifted, his whole family played. Just one of the brothers, he had about seven in the family and just one brother couldn't play. But all these little sisters and everything, the mother. Willie San Diego, the great banjo player was his uncle I think. He was that musical family. Yeah. But Bourbon could play before his feet could touch the ground. Yeah.
